entries.body: The reviewed service-manual sections do not provide a numeric bolt-length, extension, or reuse-count limit. The selected torque instruction has no final angle stage, which by itself does not establish that bolts are reusable or non-stretch. General fastener guidance recommends new bolts and says reuse, where permitted, may require expansion measurement; it gives no application-specific threshold here. A starting fixture's condition does not establish reuse permission after installation or damage. The head gasket itself is specified as new on assembly.

entries.body: Measure the head along its edges and in three directions across the center. The service procedure gives 0.05 mm as the head-warpage threshold for resurfacing consideration and 0.20 mm as the maximum resurfacing amount, subject to the stated head-height and cam-holder-clearance conditions. Measure the block deck similarly; the service table gives 0.07 mm maximum standard warpage and 0.10 mm service limit.
entries.qualification: Configuration-specific service limits; the workcell rejects parts requiring machining. entries.body: For timing-belt restoration, set No. 1 at TDC. Align the tooth-side groove on the crankshaft timing-belt drive pulley with the oil-pump pointer; align the cam-pulley TDC mark with the pointer on the timing-belt back cover and orient the pulley UP mark upward. After belt installation, rotate the crankshaft four to six turns clockwise and recheck both pulleys at TDC. Recheck the marks after timing restoration. The game phase convention is cam_phase_deg=crank_phase_deg/2 at the compression TDC datum; this is a model convention. The timing instrument accepts up to six complete crank revolutions; the correct job control uses four, matching the sourced rotation check.
entries.qualification: Summarized from the manual reproduction's timing-belt installation section; verify the exact engine variant and marks on the actual hardware.

entries.body: Service preparation requires a cold engine below 38 C, electrical isolation, drained coolant and compression TDC before head removal. The game starts with the engine cold and isolated on a service stand. External parts and the timing drive must be removed according to the delivered geometry precedence.
entries.qualification: Service-manual procedure summarized for the sourced configuration; workcell preconditions are simulation scope, not a complete vehicle repair instruction.
entries.title: Preparation and cold-engine condition

entries.body: Loosen bolts in reverse tightening order, one-third turn per bolt per pass, repeating passes until released. Each modeled bolt must be disengaged before withdrawal.
entries.qualification: The one-third-turn rule and reverse order are service-procedure facts; disengagement is the game mechanical prerequisite. Related primary OCR corroborates this instruction; exact study-CAD applicability remains unverified.
entries.title: Cylinder-head bolt removal increments

entries.body: Numbered order is 1 through 10 for tightening and 10 through 1 for loosening. In the documented layout, viewed with +Y toward the upper row and +X left-to-right, the upper row reads 8, 6, 2, 4, 10 and the lower row reads 9, 3, 1, 5, 7. Complete a whole pass in sequence order. Confirm the physical numbering against the source figure and the actual part before real service; OCR/search indexing is not visual confirmation.
entries.qualification: Sequence numbers are documented; physical figure pixels and their mapping to the reconstructed part remain unverified. Treat the spatial layout as a provisional transcription.
entries.title: Head-bolt layout and tightening order

entries.body: For the sourced fastener/application, tighten every head bolt in sequence to 30 N·m, then complete a second full pass in the same sequence to 73 N·m. No final angle stage is listed in the selected two-stage instruction. Do not finish both stages on one bolt before moving to the next. Oil the bolt threads and washer contact faces as directed by the service procedure.
entries.qualification: The selected sheet and manual text support the two torque stages. Verify the exact engine/fastener application before physical work; the service source transcription elsewhere records a 72 N·m discrepancy. Related primary OCR corroborates this instruction; exact study-CAD applicability remains unverified.
entries.title: Cylinder-head torque stages

entries.body: The reviewed service-manual sections do not provide a numeric bolt-length, extension, or reuse-count limit. The selected torque instruction has no final angle stage, which by itself does not establish that bolts are reusable or non-stretch. General fastener guidance recommends new bolts and says reuse, where permitted, may require expansion measurement; it gives no application-specific threshold here. A starting fixture's condition does not establish reuse permission after installation or damage. The head gasket itself is specified as new on assembly.
entries.qualification: Exact bolt-reuse limit could not be established. Do not infer a numeric limit or physical reuse permission from this corpus; gasket replacement is required by the service procedure.
entries.title: Head-bolt stretch and reuse status

entries.body: Measure the head along its edges and in three directions across the center. The service procedure gives 0.05 mm as the head-warpage threshold for resurfacing consideration and 0.20 mm as the maximum resurfacing amount, subject to the stated head-height and cam-holder-clearance conditions. Measure the block deck similarly; the service table gives 0.07 mm maximum standard warpage and 0.10 mm service limit.
entries.qualification: Configuration-specific service limits; the workcell rejects parts requiring machining. Confirm measurement method, head height, and cam-holder clearances in the applicable manual before repair. Related private-manual corroboration is limited to OCR text, not visual layout or geometry admission.
entries.title: Head and block flatness limits

entries.body: Protect oil and coolant openings from debris. For aluminum and multilayer-steel sealing surfaces, use a plastic scraper with a low edge angle, remove residue with a suitable cleaner, and leave clean, dry, lint-free faces. Recover debris and avoid abrasive discs, pads, grinding, or gouging. The cited general guidance does not identify an engine-specific solvent.
entries.qualification: General gasket-manufacturer preparation guidance; cleaner choice and any engine-specific restrictions require the applicable service information.
entries.title: Cleaning gasket sealing surfaces

entries.body: The gasket manufacturer recommends a surface finish of 50 RA or finer and dry installation of its multilayer-steel gasket. The source page does not state the roughness unit explicitly; do not convert this value or substitute a synthetic fixture threshold for a product specification. Use the fastener maker's specified torque.
entries.qualification: General product guidance; the roughness unit and part-specific face direction are unresolved.
entries.title: Surface finish and dry MLS installation

entries.body: The selected replacement listing specifies a 75.5 mm bore, 0.030 inch compressed thickness, and three-layer steel construction. Align the replacement on the block dowels and match its bores, fluid passages, and sealing lands. The catalog value 'Orientation: None' does not establish that the faces are reversible; the product-specific face direction remains unverified. Do not add extra sealant to the dry MLS gasket.
entries.qualification: Catalog dimensions are product-specific; correct face direction and reconstructed geometry require separate confirmation.
entries.title: Replacement head-gasket fit and orientation

entries.body: For timing-belt restoration, set No. 1 at TDC. Align the tooth-side groove on the crankshaft timing-belt drive pulley with the oil-pump pointer; align the cam-pulley TDC mark with the pointer on the timing-belt back cover and orient the pulley UP mark upward. After belt installation, rotate the crankshaft four to six turns clockwise and recheck both pulleys at TDC. Recheck the marks after timing restoration. The game phase convention is cam_phase_deg=crank_phase_deg/2 at the compression TDC datum; this is a model convention. The timing instrument accepts up to six complete crank revolutions; the correct job control uses four, matching the sourced rotation check.
entries.qualification: Summarized from the manual reproduction's timing-belt installation section; verify the exact engine variant and marks on the actual hardware.
entries.title: Timing reference marks and restoration

entries.body: Remove the cylinder-head cover before head-bolt access. The service source specifies M6 × 1.0 cover fasteners at a final 10 N·m, a new cover gasket, oil at the spark-plug tube seals, and liquid gasket at the specified end cam-holder joints. The workcell's five-fastener reverse 120-degree removal passes and intermediate 3/6 N·m passes are benchmark policies; only the 10 N·m final torque is sourced. No verified cover sequence diagram was located.
entries.qualification: Final torque and seal instructions are from the service-manual reproduction; intermediate stages, removal increments, and cover numbering are simulation-specific.
entries.title: Cylinder-head-cover removal and installation

entries.body: No verified factory numeric reuse threshold is available. This exploratory game compares permanent extension to 0.10 mm and replaces a bolt above that value. The threshold is a benchmark estimate; it must be replaced by the joint lane validated constitutive limit before physical scoring. Supplies have distinct IDs and must match the original service position.
entries.qualification: Explicit benchmark estimate; not a real-engine service specification.
entries.title: Game bolt condition convention
